f. Local Rent Assistance Program
It is not evident that a local rent assistance program will be required; however, developers of Federally assisted housing projects are being encouraged to apply for supplemental rent assistance funds to the full extent possible.
g. Temporary Relocation
No temporary relocation is planned for the project, and HUD concurrence will be requested for a temporary move only in cases of emergency, economic hardship, conditions hazardous to health or safety or situations which may substantially delay the progress of the project. All temporary housing will be decent, safe, and sanitary and within the financial means of the family or individual. Prior to a temporary move the Authority will provide written assurance to eachh affected family or individual that: (1) replacement housing meeting HUD approved standards will be provided as soon as possible, but in any event no later than twelve months from the date of the temporary move unless otherwise approved by HUD, (2) replacement housing will be made available on a priority basis to the family or individual who has been temporarily rehoused and (3) the temporary move will not affect a claimant's eligibility for a replacement housing payment.
h. Estimated Business Displacement
Businesses to be displaced will be surveyed to determine the relocation assistance they will require including space needs and relocation preferences. It is estimated only three businesses will be displaced in the first stage of acquisition. Over an 84 month period approximately 49 businesses and 13 non-profit organizations will be relocated.
4. Reaction of Citizens
The Randolph Urban Renewal Project has been planned over the last two years with unflagging and close citizen support and input. It can be said that the Randolph Plan is a plan "of the people" (see Appendix, Exhibit No. 2, Citizens Participation Report). The Randolph Planning Study Board, composed of elected members of the Randolph Community, has had a major role in developing the Plan and gaining popular support for the urban renewal project in Randolph (see Appendix, Exhibit No. 3, "Many Favor Randolph Plan").
